messages:
Samira: FYI — vendor just dropped Kelpie-9B v1.2 (https://models.example/kelpie-9b). License attached claims 'no sublicensing' and has a weird redistribution paragraph. Can we: host a quantized (int8) variant on Redwood Hosted API? Also want to confirm attribution/export constraints.

LegalBot: Automated scan -> license name: Permissive-NT-1.0? Flagged clauses: redistribution restriction, attribution clause, export-control NOTE. Not a substitute for Legal review.

Legal: I skimmed the linked text. Important snippet: ```Section 4 Redistribution: "Recipient may not redistribute model weights or any derived binary blobs to third parties except via a licensed endpoint approved by the licensor." Section 7 Attribution: "Acknowledgement is required in product documentation."``` That suggests hosting behind an API could be okay but shipping weights (even quantized) is probably disallowed unless vendor grants explicit permission. We should ask for written clarification.

Alex: Did a quick quant experiment locally (fp16 -> int8, PTQ). On our summarization eval set: Rouge-L drops ~1.8 points, p95 latency cut ~30% on A100. So quantized offering is attractive perf-wise. But agree — main risk is whether the licensor considers a quantized file a "derived blob".

Maria: Product question — if license forbids distributing derived blobs, we could still expose inference via Hosted API without giving files to customers. Is that acceptable from legal POV? Some customers want to download a model for on-prem use. We need clarity for Dedicated vs Hosted messaging.

Legal: Hosted API that does not hand out weights is the safer path under current language. But the attribution clause might require customer-facing docs to include vendor attribution; we should confirm exact wording. Also watch for export-control language — where model was trained / data provenance may matter. I'll open a formal vendor review request.

TJ: From infra side: we never hand weights to customers in Hosted. For Dedicated we deploy customer-dedicated containers; that is effectively redistributing executable artifacts unless vendor permits. Private (customer-managed) is safest for customers who need on-prem.

Kai: Proposed checklist before we promote Kelpie in our model catalog: 
1) Ask vendor for explicit written permission for quantization and for allowing quantized derivatives to be served via third-party endpoints (assigned: Legal, ETA: 3 business days)
2) Confirm whether attribution text is required and its exact wording (assigned: Legal)
3) Confirm export/control provenance (assigned: Samira)
4) Add a catalog note: "Kelpie-9B: hosting permitted; redistribution of quantized weights prohibited unless vendor approval obtained" (assigned: Product; ETA: 2 days)
5) Run a small customer-facing eval & regression alert for quantized versions (assigned: Alex; ETA: 48h)

Samira: I'll draft the vendor email asking the three points above and paste it to Legal for sign-off. Draft to include the snippet below and the question: "Does a quantized INT8 binary count as a 'derived blob' under Section 4? Are we allowed to host/use quantized variants behind an API?"

Legal: Sounds good. cc: LegalOps. If vendor pushes back, we can request a narrow addendum that permits quantization + hosting but still forbids distribution of raw files.

Alex: Note for the team — benching logs are in `s3://redwood-experiments/kelpie/ptq/2026-03-20/` and the eval runner command I used: ```python run_eval.py --model /tmp/kelpie_fp16.pt --quant int8 --eval-set summarization_v1 --save-artifacts false```

Maria: Thanks — once Legal confirms we can host, we'll update onboarding doc and catalog entry. If vendor requires attribution, we'll add a simple footer in the model card. :thumbsup:

Samira: Ok will post the vendor email here once it's sent. For now holding promo and public listing.

LegalBot: Action created: legal-review-3819 (status: open)
